cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, a family of Levite singers (2 Chronicles 20:19), and they're talking straight to God. They start with what their fathers told them: the work God did in their days, in the days of old. My boy Chip, one of my cookie cutter kids, begged me for one more story every night, and I promise you none of mine were THIS good.

cards.question: In those old stories their fathers told, what did God do to the nations living in the land?

answers.text: Drove them out with His hand
Made them friends of their fathers
Let them share the land in peace

cards.question: The singers say their fathers took the land by their own sword and the strength of their own arm.

cards.text: Not their sword, not their arm: it was God's right hand, His arm and the light of His face. Their fathers got that land the way I'd get a perfect batch handed to me while I'm still looking for the mixing bowl.

cards.question: The song says God gave their fathers the land because He ___ them.

cards.text: Then the psalmist moves from the past to right now: "You are my King, O God, who ordains victories for Jacob." Jacob is the forefather God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28).

cards.question: Now they've got enemies of their own. What does the psalmist say they're counting on to win?

cards.text: He says it straight out: he doesn't trust in his bow, and his sword doesn't save him.

They say God saves them from their enemies and puts those who hate them to shame, and they say, "In God we have boasted all day long, and Your name we will praise forever." Not a little brag here and there, friend, but ALL DAY LONG.

cards.question: Up to this point in Psalm 44, the singers have been complaining to God.

cards.text: All that praise. Then one little word flips the whole song: "But You have rejected and humbled us; You no longer go forth with our armies."

cards.question: With God no longer going out with their armies, what do the singers say happens when they face the foe?
The singers say God has given them up as sheep to be devoured. What else do they say He has done with them?

cards.text: They say God sells His people for nothing and gains no profit from the sale. Friend, I got sold for 25 cents out of a bin at a bakery that was closing, and I thought THAT was a low price tag.

cards.question: The singers say they've become a mockery to the people around them.

cards.text: They say God has made them a byword among the nations, a laughingstock among the peoples.

cards.question: Earlier, the singers boasted in God all day long. Now the psalmist says that all day long, his ___ is before him.

cards.text: Shame covers the psalmist's face at the voice of the scorner and reviler, because of the enemy, bent on revenge. This song went from a victory parade to rock bottom in eight verses.
The psalmist looks at all of it, the retreat, the plunder, the mockery, and says all this has come upon them. So here's the big question: did they bring it on themselves?

cards.question: The psalmist says all this happened because they forgot God and betrayed His covenant.

cards.text: They say their hearts have not turned back, and their steps have not strayed from God's path. These folks are holding on.

cards.question: Even so, the psalmist says God has crushed them in the lair of jackals and covered them with ___.
The psalmist says that if they had forgotten God's name or spread out their hands to a foreign god, God would have discovered it.

cards.text: He says God knows the secrets of the heart, so nobody's sneaking anything past Him. Friend, I can't even sneak one cookie off the cooling rack without the crumbs in my mustache snitching on me.

cards.question: The psalmist says they face death all day long. For whose sake?

cards.text: And the sheep come back: they say they're considered as sheep to be slaughtered. The apostle Paul quotes this line (Romans 8:36).

cards.question: The psalmist has stayed faithful, and he's still crushed. What does he cry out to God?

cards.text: Then the psalmist cries out, "Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever." I think that's a man who's hurting, and he's still talking to God.

cards.question: The psalmist asks God why He hides His face.

cards.text: He asks why God forgets their affliction and oppression. I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: The psalmist says their soul has sunk to the ___ and their bodies cling to the earth.
Down in the dust, the psalmist asks God to rise up and redeem them. On account of what?

cards.text: "Rise up; be our help! Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion." And the song ends right there, still calling out to God.
